subject.title: fix(gateway): preserve abort after dispatch rejection

question: Should explicit `chat.abort` always outrank a later dispatch rejection, while an accepted queued followup remains terminal unless an explicit abort marker owns the run?
rationale: The reported abort-overwrite behavior is clearly a bug, but this PR also defines permanent client-visible precedence for simultaneous followup, interruption, and rejection states; source inspection cannot determine that product contract without Gateway owner intent.

options.title: Approve Proposed Precedence
options.body: Treat explicit abort as terminal owner, otherwise preserve an accepted queued followup, and let dispatch error own all remaining rejection cases.

options.title: Narrow To Abort Preservation
options.body: Keep only abort-before-rejection preservation and defer broader followup and lifecycle-interruption precedence to separate owner-reviewed work.

recommendation.title: Approve Proposed Precedence
recommendation.body: Treat explicit abort as terminal owner, otherwise preserve an accepted queued followup, and let dispatch error own all remaining rejection cases.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the current lifecycle-admission and dispatch-error behavior immediately surrounding the changed path.
